title: Easy Chat
subtitle: Full Stack Web App
description: Easy Chat is a browser-based web messenger engineered for seamless, real-time communication without requiring heavy app downloads. The application features direct user-to-user messaging, inline media sharing, dynamic message controls (edit, replace, or delete), and full profile management. Built directly into the browser, it highlights clean front-end architecture, state management, and responsive UI design—delivering a fast, intuitive chat platform accessible on any device.
details:
### Easy Chat: Architectural & Technical Deep Dive

### Overview & Core Architecture

Easy Chat was built from the ground up to explore real-time web architecture without relying on heavy third-party UI framework state tools like Redux. Instead, state management across the application is engineered entirely around React’s Context API, keeping data flow predictable while keeping bundle sizes light.

### Real-Time Infrastructure with WebSockets

To enable instant, low-latency communication between devices across the web, the platform relies on Socket.io. Every message transmission, status update, and session event is handled through custom event-driven WebSockets, maintaining persistent full-duplex connections across client browsers.

$$0$$

### Creative Media Handling & Upload Pipelines

Handling images in real-time messaging often bloats payload sizes and strains server bandwidth. To solve this, Easy Chat delegates heavy media hosting to Cloudinary via client-side integration.

When a user attaches an image, the client compresses and uploads the asset directly to Cloudinary, receiving back a secure CDN URL. Instead of streaming heavy binary files through the WebSocket server, the app sends light text payloads containing the image reference and metadata. Special token markers in the message parser allow the front end to conditionally render full dynamic image components alongside standard text seamlessly.

$$1$$

$$2$$

### Custom AI Integration & System Prompting

To enhance user interaction, Easy Chat includes an embedded AI assistant powered by Llama models via a custom API endpoint. Rather than implementing heavy context models, the system features a light UI tagging system that appends smart instruction prompts to user queries behind the scenes:

- **Text Enhancement Tags:** Modifies the outgoing payload to enforce detailed, natural language formatting from the model.

- **Code Mode Tags:** Appends strict structural directives to force the LLM to output clean, raw code blocks rather than conversational prose.

$$3$$

$$4$$

### Session Management & Performance Optimizations

User persistence and seamless browsing were primary design goals. The front-end architecture implements a custom caching mechanism alongside browser session tracking. This ensures instant data loading during re-renders, minimizes redundant API fetches, and keeps active chat sessions synchronized across multiple browser tabs.

$$5$$

$$6$$

### Lightweight Node.js Backend & In-Memory Data Strategy

The backend service is built on Node.js and hosted on Render. It orchestrates active user profiles, session validation, and real-time socket channels.

$$7$$

To maintain high performance during testing, the database architecture utilizes an in-memory SQL strategy. While runtime storage reset during server deployments presented unique challenges, it ensured zero storage latency for message routing and quick session handling.

$$8$$

### Tech Stack

- **Frontend:** TypeScript • React 19 (Context API) • React Router v7 • Framer Motion • Bootstrap 5

- **Backend:** Node.js • Express v5 • Socket.io • JWT • bcrypt

- **Database & Cloud:** Turso (LibSQL/SQLite) • Cloudinary • Render • GitHub Pages

- **Key Utilities:** Axios • Browser-Image-Compression

title: Easy Park
subtitle: 3D / Animation
description: Easy Park is a 3D animated concept trailer for a mobile app designed to resolve urban parking gridlock. Built around a license plate scanning system that lets drivers instantly notify owners of blocked vehicles, the project was modeled, staged, and rendered in Blender to demonstrate motion design, camera composition, and app store promotional visualization.
details:
### Easy Park: 3D Product Visualization & Animation Pipeline

### Project Origin & Strategic Vision

Easy Park began as a business capstone project designed to address high-density urban parking gridlock in Armenia. To effectively communicate the business model to academic evaluators, potential investors, and government stakeholders—whose cooperation would be necessary for license plate database access—the project required more than a static pitch deck.
The goal was to engineer a high-impact, 3D promotional trailer within a strict one-week production window, serving as an app store video showcase and proof of concept.

$$0$$

### Environment Staging & Scene Optimization

Built for high-fidelity visual output rather than real-time game performance, the complete 3D environment contained over 1,861,000 triangles. To maintain rapid production velocity without reinventing base assets, existing 3D models were integrated, restructured, and optimized for the scene.

- **Shader & Material Reconstruction:** Imported assets were stripped of broken dependencies and rebuilt. Materials were re-linked, adjusted, and blended using custom procedural shaders inside Blender's Shader Editor.

- **Scene Clean-up:** Extravagant vehicle details were pruned, and materials were unified to establish a consistent, realistic urban aesthetic across the entire set.

$$1$$

$$2$$

### Cinematic Camera Work & Motion Tracking

To give the trailer the polished feel of a commercial advertisement, the camera animation relied heavily on dynamic lenses, depth-of-field manipulation, and motion constraints.

- **Dynamic Lens Selection:** Focal lengths were altered continuously throughout the sequence—ranging from wide 27mm environmental framing to tight 136mm telephoto tracking shots—to direct viewer attention.

- **Cinematic Focus & Motion Tracking:** Cameras were parented to character joint rigs and vehicle paths, utilizing continuous depth-of-field tracking to switch focus between the driver, the vehicle, and the mobile UI in real time.

$$3$$

$$4$$

### Creative UI Compositing & Handheld Simulation

Rather than building complex in-engine 3D interface animations, a hybrid screen-mapping workflow was executed:

1. **Transparent UI Masking:** The mobile device’s viewport screen was modeled with a transparent camera region inside the UI overlay.

2. **Video Texture Mapping:** Pre-recorded footage was mapped directly as an animated material texture onto the 3D phone screen inside Blender.

3. **Micro-Shake Simulation:** Subtle procedural noise and camera shake were keyframed into the 3D phone rig to simulate organic handheld movement, ensuring the digital UI felt naturally embedded in the physical scene.

$$5$$

$$6$$

### Lighting, Cycles Rendering & Post-Production

To achieve realistic outdoor lighting, the scene combined HDRI environment maps with a directional Sun Light and supplemental 3-point studio lighting for character keying.

- **Render Engine:** Rendered entirely in Cycles at 1080p / 24 fps to ensure physical light transport, glass refraction, and accurate vehicle paint reflections.

- **Editorial & Post-Processing:** Final render passes were exported from Blender into external video editing software for final color grading, pacing edits, audio synchronization, and post-effects.

$$7$$

$$8$$

### Tools & Technologies Used
- **3D Software:** Blender (Cycles Render Engine, Shader Editor, Camera Tracking)

- **Lighting & Materials:** HDRI Environmental Lighting • Procedural Shading • PBR Material Repair

- **Cinematics & VFX:** Dynamic Focal Lengths (27mm–136mm) • Motion Constraints • Video Texture Mapping

- **Production & Pipeline:** Rapid Prototyping (1-Week Sprint) • Post-Production Color Grading • 1080p / 24fps Output

title: HK416
subtitle: 3D / Animation
description: A detailed 3D model of a modern assault rifle inspired by the HK416 platform, created as a high-fidelity digital asset for visualization and animation purposes. It includes multiple visualization variants such as solid, textured, UV-mapped, and topology-focused versions, making it suitable for both rendering and study of structure and form.
details: The model was created in Blender and consists of 40,991 triangles. It includes a fully rigged bone system designed to simulate realistic firearm mechanics, allowing for full animation of components such as the trigger and other movable parts. The asset was built with clean topology and UV mapping to support different rendering workflows, including textured and non-textured (solid) visual modes. It is optimized for animation, with a fully controllable rig that allows realistic motion simulation of firearm operation within 3D environments.

title: Thomas
subtitle: 3D / Animation
description: This project is a fully handcrafted 3D character asset produced across two distinct outfit and styling variants. Built from the ground up—including custom hair, apparel, and canvas high-top sneakers—the character features complete custom UV mapping, hand-authored PBR textures, and a full body rig. The project highlights clean mesh construction, detailed material creation, and production-ready asset optimization for games or cinematic renders.
details:
### Thomas: High-Detail 3D Character & Game-Ready Asset Pipeline

### Anatomical Sculpting & Topology Preservation

The character foundation was built leveraging the MPFB framework, followed by custom sculpting passes in Blender to adjust facial proportions, jaw structure, eye placement, and hand anatomy for a 27–30-year-old male aesthetic.

Rather than destroying the base mesh through dynamic topology remeshing, vertex positions were adjusted directly in Sculpt Mode. This preserved the production-ready edge loops—maintaining clean, circular loops around the eyes, mouth, shoulders, and joints critical for real-time deformation.

$$0$$

$$1$$

### Garment Construction & Custom Footwear Modeling

Garment geometry was engineered using a combination of mesh extraction and hand-modeling:

- **Trousers, T-Shirt, & Hoodie Body:** Extruded directly from the underlying body topology. Reusing the base edge flow ensured proper garment alignment and prevented clipping, while the hood element was built by hand to achieve proper spatial volume.

- **Handcrafted High-Top Sneakers:** Built from scratch starting with the sole, extruding upward to construct the thick rubber rand, heel cup, and canvas upper. The right and left shoes feature asymmetrical anatomical shaping, smooth merged seams, and separate lace geometry.

$$2$$

$$3$$

### Hand-Placed Hair Cards & PBR Material Pipeline

To deliver real-time hair without the performance cost of particle systems, individual hair cards were placed by hand across the scalp, eyebrows, and beard.

- **Texture Authoring:** Initial procedural node materials were authored in Blender, then converted into game-ready PBR texture maps (Base Color, Normal, Roughness, Specular, and Alpha) utilizing the Ravage add-on.

- **Optimization:** Subsurface scattering was bypassed in favor of baked high-poly details in the Normal map, keeping shader execution lightweight for game engines.

$$4$$

$$5$$

### Skeletal Rigging, Weight Painting, & Studio Renders

The asset was fitted with a standard skeletal armature to ensure seamless movement across animation pipelines.

- **Weight Map Painting:** Rig weights across the hoodie and canvas sneakers were manually repainted to fix mesh floating and garment clipping issues common with default auto-weighting.

- **Studio Lighting Setup:** Renders were executed inside a light-isolated black enclosure using a controlled 3-point studio lighting setup (Key, Fill, and Rim lights) to highlight form, material roughness, and specular highlights without background light bounce.

$$6$$

title: K-45P (Usp Tactical)
subtitle: 3D / Animation
description: K-45P (USP Tactical) is a game-ready weapon asset built in Blender and textured in Substance Painter. Designed to build instant visual interest, the showcase highlights PBR textures, UV unwrapped layout, and wireframe projection views demonstrating clean quad topology.
details:
The USP Tactical (K-45P) project was structured around building an efficient, game-ready asset that balances high visual fidelity with clean technical execution. This technical breakdown covers the topology, PBR layer composition, and custom pipeline workflows used to develop the weapon in Blender and Substance Painter.

$$0$$

### Direct Modeling & Topology Optimization

Rather than relying on a traditional high-to-low blockout pass, the mesh was built through a direct reference-shaping workflow—starting from primary rough forms and progressively subdividing into production topology. The final mesh is optimized for real-time engine constraints (supporting both first-person and third-person camera views):

- **Faces:** ~4,000
- **Triangles:** 7,415
- **Vertices:** 8,382

Heavy reliance on symmetry modifiers streamlined early geometric density, while quad redirection was manually applied around complex stress areas—such as slide serrations, the trigger guard, and the ejection port—to maintain smooth shading and clean edge highlights.



$$1$$

### UV Unwrapping & Texel Density

To ensure maximum texel density on primary player-facing surfaces while minimizing visible seams, UV islands were logically grouped across the primary frame, attachments, optical glass, and ammunition. Seams were aligned along natural geometric breaks, hard-surface bevels, and undercarriage tracks.



$$2$$

### Physical Material Definition & PBR Layering

Texturing was executed in Substance Painter, using 4K map sets for the firearm and attachments, along with dedicated 512p maps for the ammunition. The weapon is divided into distinct physical material definitions:

1. **Textured Polymer:** Applied to the frame and grip, featuring micro-stippling grain, organic roughness variations, and subtle surface wear.
2. **Anodized Aluminum:** Used for the slide and mechanical assemblies, capturing realistic metallic highlights and light scattering.
3. **Matte Darkened Aluminum:** Applied to tactical attachments, featuring heavier edge wear, scuffs, and distinct roughness variations.
4. **Glass & Emissive Sights:** Clear refractive glass shaders paired with green emissive maps for the tactical sights, flashlight, and laser module.



$$3$$

### Material Iteration & Surface Detail Tuning

Achieving photorealistic response on the anodized aluminum required significant iteration. Initial shaders appeared flat, leading to a complete rebuild of the material stack over two weeks. Height micro-stippling, ambient occlusion overlays, and custom roughness channels were repeatedly fine-tuned to match real-world physical behavior.



$$4$$

### Custom Pipeline Tooling: Texture Atlas & Draw Call Consolidation

Splitting the firearm across four distinct materials initially produced 28 individual texture maps (Base Color, Roughness, Metallic, Normal, Height, Opacity, AO, and Emissive). Importing these into game engines created excessive draw calls and material management overhead.

To automate texture packing without manually combining maps in photo editing software, I designed and built a dedicated custom utility application. This software programmatically packs and consolidates all 28 individual texture maps into a single, optimized 7-map PBR material set.

Learn more about how this custom texture automation tool was built here: [View Texture Consolidation Tool Project](link:7).



$$5$$

### Full Mesh Wireframe Analysis

Analyzing the final wireframe overlay demonstrates the distribution of support loops, edge flow, and quad continuity across both the main weapon frame and modular attachments.



$$6$$

### PBR Texture Channel Breakdown

An isolated view of the packed PBR channels demonstrates how individual roughness masks, metallic parameters, normal maps, and height details work together to create realistic surface response under dynamic lighting.



$$7$$
